Maya: Heads-up from today's onboarding: Cynosure-6B int4 conversion shows stable short outputs but severe position-dependent divergence after ~3072 tokens. FP16 ppl 9.7, int4 ppl jumps to 18.2 past 3k. Any ideas? :confounded:
Ethan: Position-dependent makes me think rotary freq/base or a padding/sentinel reuse. Did the converter preserve any positional config?
Maya: Converter log excerpt: 
```
[INFO] reading config.json
[WARN] rotary_scale: not found, defaulting to 1.0
[INFO] vocab written to converted/vocab.json (ordering preserved: false)
```
Model config: `{"rotary_freq": 4096, "rotary_scale": 1.37, "vocab_size": 50688}`
Zoe: "vocab ordering preserved: false" is a red flag. If vocab order changed but tokenizer still encodes to old indices, embeddings and KV alignments break. Also rotary_scale mismatch will rotate at wrong frequency.
Liam: Also saw a pattern: some in-domain texts with CJK + zero-width joiners produced tokens mapped to id 2 (reserved EOS) during conversion tests. Example: 
```
>>> tokenizer.encode("研究\u200d文")
[345, 2, 78]
```
That EOS in-stream will truncate or shift KV positions.
Ethan: Two independent problems compounding: vocabs remapped + invisible-control chars yielding sentinel IDs + rotary scale mismatch. Fix path: 1) force converter to roundtrip vocab ordering exactly (preserve indices), 2) ensure converter reads `rotary_freq` and `rotary_scale` keys and surfaces them, 3) strip/re-normalize control chars or map them consistently.
Maya: Quick repro commands I ran: 
```
python tools/convert.py --src cynosure6b/ --dst converted/cynosure6b-int4/ --quant q4_0 --backend gptq
python tools/rotary_probe.py --model converted/cynosure6b-int4/ --maxlen 8192
```
rotary_probe output: 
```
[WARN] head 2: wrap_pos 3072 delta 0.29 rad
[WARN] head 8: wrap_pos 4096 delta 0.45 rad
```
Ethan: After forcing `rotary_freq=4096` in the converted config and re-converting with `--preserve-vocab-order` I got much better behavior: ppl down to 11.8 and no early wrap. But there were still occasional EOS-id insertions when input contained ASCII NUL or other control codepoints.
Zoe: For control codes, I suggest adding a sanitizer step in the tokenizer pipeline: normalize to NFKC and explicitly remove codepoints in category Cc except newline/tab. Also add a CI tokenization roundtrip test that samples from the training corpus and ensures encode->decode preserves textual graphemes.
Liam: Also try asymmetric quant in gptq; symmetric quant with clamp can bias attentions for some heads. Command that helped: 
```
python tools/convert.py --src cynosure6b/ --dst converted/cynosure6b-int4-asym/ --quant q4_0 --quant-mode asymmetric --preserve-vocab-order --preserve-rotary
```
That produced int4 ppl 10.9 and longctx stable to 8k in my smoke.
Maya: Infra artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/eng-ml/1729991234/cynosure-convert.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Ethan: Action items: 1) Patch converter to accept rotary keys (`rotary_freq`, `rotary.base`, `rotary_emb.base`) and rotary_scale aliases, 2) Make `--preserve-vocab-order` default for onboards, 3) Add tokenizer sanitizer removing Cc except 
	allowed = {9,10,13}, 4) Add `rotary_probe` to onboarding CI and fail if any head wrap_pos < context_len with delta >0.05 rad.
Zoe: I'll own the tokenizer sanitizer PR and add roundtrip tests for CJK+ZWJ and control chars.
Liam: I'll add an asymmetric-gptq conversion path in convert.py and an automated smoke that runs the three quant modes (symmetric/asymmetric/per-channel) and picks best longctx perf.
Maya: Filed tickets: RED-4020 (converter rotary+vocab), RED-4021 (tokenizer Cc sanitizer), RED-4022 (onboard rotary_probe CI). Thanks team. :sparkles:
